solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Film magazine next to old folio paper (6,2,3,3)

indicatorNotes.next to: means placed beside, so the magazine sits directly before the letters that follow it

blocks.note: Empire is a British film magazine
O = old, as in OE for Old English
The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper

annotation.surface: A film magazine sitting beside a stack of old folio paper.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'film magazine' one phrase, but 'Film' alone is the definition and the magazine is the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Spielberg's 1987 wartime drama about a boy interned in Shanghai is one particular film.

entries.clue: This writer’s diamonds dug up (5)

annotation.surface: Someone boasting that the diamonds unearthed belong to them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter speaking of themself, and the surface of diamonds being dug up points straight at the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: ore or gems extracted from underground workings have been mined.

entries.clue: Cold-blooded type, half-cut, aims a gun recklessly (6)

indicatorNotes.half-cut: a word cut in half keeps only half its letters, so AIMS keeps AI
indicatorNotes.recklessly: done without care, so the letters land in any order

blocks.note: AIMS with its second half cut off

annotation.surface: A drunk, heartless thug waving a gun about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' reads as drunk, and 'cold-blooded type' as a ruthless person; both mislead.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal sense: reptiles such as this lizard cannot make their own body heat, while the surface wants cold-blooded to mean callous.

entries.clue: Seven pull out after drug test (6-4)

indicatorNotes.out: out of order, so the letters of SEVEN PULL are rearranged
indicatorNotes.after: places the rearranged letters after the drug's letter

annotation.surface: Seven athletes withdraw after a drug test.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a doping scandal, and 'test' is its natural last word, so the exam hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Specific instance: the English exam sat around age eleven that decided entry to grammar schools is a test.

entries.clue: Iron clothes before midday for celebrity (4)

indicatorNotes.clothes: to clothe is to dress, to wrap round, so the iron letters go round the time

blocks.note: Fe, the chemical symbol for iron

annotation.surface: Ironing your clothes before noon to look your best in the spotlight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Iron' and 'clothes' read as laundry; 'clothes' is a verb here, and iron is the element.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: celebrity as a condition, being widely known and talked about, is renown.

entries.clue: What about new supermarket eggs here? (3-4)

indicatorNotes.about: to turn about is to face the other way, so EH is read backwards

blocks.note: the Co-op, a British supermarket chain

annotation.surface: A shopper asking whether the new supermarket stocks eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'eggs here' is a playful definition: the place eggs are laid, not sold.
annotation.definitionFit: Playful description: the hutch where laying birds live is where fresh eggs turn up.

entries.clue: Photo that includes mum good for ego (4-5)

indicatorNotes.includes: something that includes another holds it inside, so the photo wraps round the next letters

annotation.surface: A selfie with Mum in it gives someone's confidence a lift.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface photo is itself a vanity exercise, which suits a clue about ego.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: ego is one's sense of who one is, how a person sees and values themselves.

entries.clue: Husband visiting prime hotel, amazing bar after lots of driving (10,4)

indicatorNotes.visiting: a visitor goes inside, so H is put into the rearranged HOTEL
indicatorNotes.amazing: lost in a maze, so HOTEL's letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A husband staying at a top hotel with a fabulous bar after a long drive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Driving' is golf, not motoring, and 'prime' is a noun, a prime number.
annotation.definitionFit: Golfing slang: a course has eighteen holes, so the clubhouse bar players retire to after a round is jokingly the next one.

entries.clue: Be a little mad? It won’t be Thatcher’s fault! (4,1,4,5)

blocks.note: British slang for being slightly crazy
a thatcher roofs with straw, so a slipped roof tile is someone else's problem

annotation.surface: A sly jab at Margaret Thatcher: whatever the madness, don't blame her.
annotation.walkthrough: Thatcher looks like the Prime Minister, but it is a tradesman who roofs houses with straw.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a loose slate or tile suggests something not quite secure upstairs, hence mild madness; literally it is a roofing fault no thatcher could cause.

entries.clue: American doctor a man sued time after time, annoyingly (2,7)

indicatorNotes.doctor: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

annotation.surface: An American doctor who is sued over and over again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb, not the American's job, and 'time after time' is part of the definition rather than a T.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin phrase: literally 'to sickness', used of something repeated until everyone is sick of it.

entries.clue: Material from journo Lynam rejected (5)

indicatorNotes.from: taken from inside the words, so the letters are already in the clue
indicatorNotes.rejected: sent back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: sitting across journO LYNam, then turned round

annotation.surface: A piece written by the journalist Lynam gets turned down.
annotation.walkthrough: Des Lynam is a British sports broadcaster; his name is there only to carry the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Category member: the synthetic polymer used for stockings and rope is a textile, a material.

entries.clue: Risk when close by firework, losing head (8)

indicatorNotes.by: means beside, so the first part sits next to the second
indicatorNotes.losing head: the head of a word is its first letter, which is lost

blocks.note: BANGER without its B; a banger is a loud firework

annotation.surface: Standing too close to a firework is a risk that could cost you your head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close' reads as an adjective, near; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to risk something is to expose it to harm or loss.

entries.clue: Council very, very inept, oddly (6)

indicatorNotes.oddly: in an odd way, read as the odd-numbered positions, so the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters are kept

annotation.surface: A complaint that the local council is hopelessly incompetent.
annotation.walkthrough: The repeated 'very' is two different words, a word and an abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Russian loanword: an elected workers' assembly in the USSR, the word literally meaning council.

entries.clue: Creature, small dog in wicker basket (7,3)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another is inside it, so the dog goes into the basket

blocks.note: a creel is an angler's wicker basket
a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

annotation.surface: A little dog curled up in a wicker basket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small dog' reads as one thing, a little dog, but 'small' works alone as a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Category: a small American owl named for its shrill call is an animal, a creature.

entries.clue: Lift drink with ice at last (4)

indicatorNotes.at last: at the end, so only the final letter is used
indicatorNotes.with: along with, so the two parts are joined

blocks.note: a tot is a small drink

annotation.surface: Raising a glass of something on the rocks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like raising a glass; it means carry.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to carry something heavy about, lugging it along, is what lifting it off the ground begins.

entries.clue: Conductor to glance over popular first part of intermezzo (9)

indicatorNotes.first part of: the first part of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to scan is to glance over

annotation.surface: A conductor looking over the score of an intermezzo.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface fits the answer, so the solver is steered right while the pieces stay hidden.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Arturo, the Italian maestro of La Scala and the NBC orchestra, led orchestras.

entries.clue: Discovery perhaps of accommodation – flat (10)

blocks.note: a plane is a flat surface

annotation.surface: Finding somewhere to live, possibly a flat.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is house-hunting; Discovery is the NASA shuttle, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: NASA's shuttle orbiter rode a rocket into orbit and glided down to a runway.

entries.clue: Barrister’s failures outside court, essentially things not worth pursuing (4,6)

indicatorNotes.outside: one thing outside another surrounds it
indicatorNotes.essentially: in essence, at its core, so only the central letter is used

annotation.surface: A barrister's defeats outside court, basically not worth the fight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court' seems to be where the barrister works; only its central letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a cause already doomed to fail is not worth further effort.

entries.clue: Abrupt trick taking in university team (7)

indicatorNotes.Abrupt: abrupt means cut short, so the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.taking in: to take in is to hold inside, so the university goes within

blocks.note: CHEAT with its end cut off

annotation.surface: A curt con that fools a university side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abrupt' looks like an adjective describing the trick; it is the instruction to cut it short.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the West London football club is a sports team.

entries.clue: Plates in area of London cost tons (4)

annotation.surface: Dinner plates in a London district costing a fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang is the dialect of London's East End.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: 'plates of meat' rhymes with the body part, and is shortened to 'plates'.

entries.clue: Way ultimately ruthless leader of Tories stifles Redwood? (6)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: in the end, so the final letter is used
indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader goes first, so the opening letter is used
indicatorNotes.stifles: to stifle is to smother, so the two letters close round the tree

blocks.note: a redwood is an example of a tree

annotation.surface: A merciless Tory leader silencing John Redwood.
annotation.walkthrough: John Redwood is a Conservative MP, which makes the political surface; the question mark shows he is standing in for a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a road, as in names like Abbey Road or Fish Street.

entries.clue: Might we be moved by The Rake’s Progress? Parts (6)

annotation.definition2: Might we be moved by The Rake’s Progress?

blocks.clueFragment: Might we be moved by The Rake’s Progress?
blocks.note: what a garden rake sweeps along the lawn in autumn

annotation.surface: Wondering whether a famous work of art could stir us, then going.
annotation.walkthrough: The Rake's Progress is Hogarth's picture series and Stravinsky's opera, but here a garden rake progresses across a lawn.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: someone who parts company goes away, and fallen foliage is what a rake gathers.

entries.clue: Gladiator director is initially hiding from Harris? (8)

indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so only the first letter is used

annotation.surface: A film director hiding from someone called Harris.
annotation.walkthrough: Harris looks like a person; it is an island, and the question mark flags it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Harris is an island in the Outer Hebrides, off Scotland's north-west coast, so its people are Scots.

entries.clue: Everything included where Eve goes for examination (2,3)

blocks.note: EVE slotted between A and LL spells A-LEVEL, the English school-leaving exam

annotation.surface: Eve being told to undress completely for a medical.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a recipe read backwards: it describes where three letters go to make an exam, and that position is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Two readings: all told, as a total; and the placement that turns A-LL into the exam taken at eighteen.

entries.clue: Upset, jobless regularly, zero capital (4)

indicatorNotes.Upset: knocked over, so in a down clue the letters read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter is used

annotation.surface: Out of work and broke, with nothing to one's name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, next to jobless and zero; it is a city.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Norway's seat of government is a capital city.

entries.clue: They have passed subjects (5)

blocks.note: the surface reading: students who got through their exams; the meant reading: people who have died
the surface reading: school subjects; the meant reading: the people a piece of writing is about

annotation.surface: Students who have got through their exams.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passed' sounds like exam success; here it means passed away.
annotation.definitionFit: Newspaper death notices, short for obituaries, take as their subjects people who have died.

entries.clue: Bat defensively as not well when running (9)

indicatorNotes.running: colours running blur into new shapes, so the letters move into a new order

annotation.surface: A cricketer batting cautiously because they feel too ill to run.
annotation.walkthrough: The cricket surface fits the answer, and 'running' looks like running between the wickets.
annotation.definitionFit: Cricket term: a batter who blocks every ball without trying to score is building a wall in front of the stumps.

entries.clue: Flower girl getting help, in a manner of speaking? (5,9)

annotation.definition: Flower girl getting help, in a manner of speaking?

blocks.note: the surface reading: a bridesmaid being assisted; the meant reading: the Covent Garden flower seller taking lessons
the surface reading: so to speak; the meant reading: the help is with her manner of speaking, her accent

annotation.surface: A young bridesmaid being given a hand, more or less.
annotation.walkthrough: She is the Cockney heroine of Shaw's Pygmalion and the musical My Fair Lady, taught to speak 'properly' by Professor Higgins.
annotation.definitionFit: Literary character: Shaw's Covent Garden flower seller receives elocution lessons, help with how she speaks.
